No retired clause is stated as in force; no clause is retired that the source does not retire.

## kb_to_source

- Every normative claim in the 86 documents traced to a source atom (base rule, variant parameter or its schema description, event/measure definition, extended rule, factor ladder or tool contract). Derived restatements checked and found entailed: "What the customer says about these matters does not replace the records" (enrollment/holding/rescission docs) ← `evidence_contract.authority: system_record`; "The credit being worked out is not yet on the bill and is not counted" (referral_count_bonus) ← compute counts pre-posting lines; "An agreement with no contract end date has no expiring term and receives none" (commitment) ← compute guard; "On a time-of-use agreement the on-peak and off-peak lines are each one line" (usage/volume) ← COUNT of energy_charge lines; "billed supply balance" (supply_charge_billing_standard) ← `accounts.supply_billed`.
- Additions: none found. Omissions: none found. Rewrites changing meaning: none found.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none. The only tool names in the corpus are each exclusive tool inside its own hub's invocation block (exact scan: each of the 8 task tools appears in exactly one document, its own hub).
- A task's opening world state written as a policy fact: none. Worked figures are hypothetical and do not reproduce this task's rows (no 2026-07-01 gap, no 11.89/10.89 rates, no Owen/Diane figures).

Policy-side notes (nature recorded; not a KB verdict):
- `power_renewal` keeps the base clause "A late election is not a renewal; the customer may instead change plans under the plan change policy at the then-valid price offer" (rendered verbatim in renewal_election_terms rule 5), while `power_ext_plan_change_rate` re-prices every plan change from the contract rate in force "rather than the price-sheet offer" and retires only the `power_plan_change_terms` pricing clause. Undeclared tension between a base clause and an extended override; the KB renders both faithfully. Not on this task's path.
- `events.power_renew.fields.contract_rate_cents_kwh` ("The renewal rate offered in the renewal notice") is the pre-override field meaning; schema text, not rendered in the KB, no effect.
- The renewal notice's stated contract end date is the record field `effective_date` (`events.power_renewal_notice.fields.effective_date: "The contract_end_date the notice refers to"`). The KB names it "the contract end date printed on that notice" / "stated on its latest renewal notice" without naming the record field; in this world the notice's effective_date equals the agreement's end date, so the reading is unique. Findability note only.
- "billing dispute lookback" (source term, carried verbatim in the prerequisite sentence and dual_fuel_credit_rules rule 4) vs "Billing correction lookback (calendar months before the dispute date)" (the KB's rendering of `billing_dispute_lookback_months`). One lookback exists (12 months on every plan) and the header names the dispute date, so entailment holds; wording note only. How the lookback applies to a never-posted cycle is not defined in the source either.
